comment: One row for each rule of rule (b) of D17.21, a use after `move` or `del`, in the proof of
src/fort/owner/prover.ft: the operations that vacate an owner, the places that overlap it, the
borrows of a place through a pointer, the events that end the state and the keys that undo an
end, the edge of a test against null, the reads that are uses and the reads that are not, the
order inside one statement, the join and the loops, the owner that a use names, the operation of
its note, and the limit of the work. Then the owners of a local and the keys of src/fort/owner/
place.ft, the lines of the report of rule (b) in src/fort/owner/report.ft, and the option
--move-report of src/fort/driver.ft. D17.21-error makes rule (b) an error, which no build gives
yet. The first stage runs the cases over FIR text (test/fort/owner/prover_use_test.ft) and the
lines of the report over lowered fort source (test/fort/owner/report_use_test.ft). The second
runs the driver test, which holds the lines of --move-report and that rule (b) changes no status.
The third runs the oracle test, which prints a false accept of rule (b) for a row that makes the
pass prove a use that a run reads after a `move` or a `del`. The table runs in the Linux VM with
the debug preset and the default runner. The md5 guard reads the product compiler, whose driver
imports owner.prover and owner.report. The first round of a run can read stale
(notes/testing.md 7), so the first row is one that a full run caught.

stages.name: the module tests of rule (b)
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 2 owner/prover_use_test owner/report_use_test

stages.name: the driver test
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 2 driver_test

stages.name: the oracle test
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 2 owner/oracle_test

mutations.old: vacate_act(c, u, i, s->place, at, stale);
mutations.what: a `del` vacates no owner

mutations.old: vacate_act(c, u, i, o.place, at, stale);
mutations.what: a `move` operand vacates no owner, also the implicit `move` of `return x`
a call vacates no memory owner
a `move` or a `del` vacates only the owner that it names: no other element of a fixed array and no owner below its place

mutations.old: bool reached = aliased == null || alias.can_be(&c->aliases, aliased, a->path, x);
mutations.what: a `move` or a `del` through a pointer vacates no memory owner
a read through a pointer uses no memory owner
a store into a place with a local key ends the state for good, also when a store into the key follows
a store into a key undoes no end
a store into a key undoes only the ends that hold a later key too
a store into a part of an owner, such as the `.len` of a span, ends its state
the edge where a test finds null ends the state, and the edge of another value does not

mutations.old:
copy_values(w->edge, w->s);
            apply_act(c, u, a, &w->aliased, w->edge);
mutations.new:
copy_values(w->edge, w->s);
            apply_act(c, u, a, &w->aliased, w->s);
mutations.what: a test against null ends the state on each edge
an operation between the read of a test and its branch vacates nothing on the edge
a comparison with any value, not only null, is no use
a read of a `.len` through a pointer is no use
the read of the value of an operand is no use
the reads of the pointers of an access path are no uses: `*p` and `p->f` use no `p`

mutations.old:
pointer_acts(c, u, i, s->place, stale);
    bool fixed =
mutations.what: the pointers that the destination of a store loads are no reads
a `return` reads no `_0`
`check(overwrite: p)` reads no pointer of the address of `p`
a block starts with no operation of its predecessors: no union join
the fixpoint walks each block once, so no operation goes around a back edge
a charge equal to the limit passes it
the first pass of a function past the limit makes its state
the limit of the work of rule (b) is 2^20 and not 2^24
a read of a part of an owner, such as its `.ptr`, is no use of it
a read with an index that is no key uses no owner
a use names the first owner of its local, and not the first that can be vacated
the note names the last operation in the order of the source positions
the note of a `del` says that the owner is moved
the analysis proves each use
a function with no operation that vacates reads the owners that it never made
an unproved use of rule (b) is a compile error, which no build gives yet
each element of a fixed array of owners of a local is the owner at index 0
the rank of a key names the first key that is another local
the message of rule (b) takes the text of the design and not that of D17.21
the note of a `move` says that the owner is deleted
the note of a `del` says that the owner is moved

mutations.old: strbuf.append(out, "' can change in this call\n");
mutations.what: the note of a call says that the owner is moved
the error stands at the operand of a `move` that reads the same place before the use
a deferred use gives one line for each exit
the first line past the limit takes no note of the limit
the note of a call stands at its parenthesis and not at its first token
the note of the implicit `move` of `return x` stands at `x` and not at the `return`
the result `_0` is named by the name of the function alone
a read that no source expression names gives the FIR place
the error stands at the item and not at the first token of the expression
the error stands at the operand of a comparison with null that reads the same place first
--move-report lists no use
--move-report alone prints nothing
--move-report runs --check and lists nothing
a place through a global names no owner, also when the global holds the address of a memory local
past the limit a read through a pointer takes a rank in the type of the memory local
an owner that a read with a local key names takes twice its values
the count of the values goes on after the key of a read passes the limit, so the fixpoint, and not the first pass, stops
the owners below a read count with their keys also when they alone pass the limit
a global in fixed storage names an owner when a memory local holds one
